svg.title: One stretch, counted twice
svg.desc: From the division of the kingdom in 931 BC to Jehu's revolt in 841 BC, when Joram of Israel and Ahaziah of Judah were killed in one chase (2 Kings 9:24, 27). Four rows on one scale of years. Israel's reigns as Kings numbers them, laid end to end: 98 years, running 8 years past Jehu. The same reigns on the calendar after Thiele: each king's first year was also his predecessor's last, so each reign carries one year counted twice, 8 in all, and they end at 841 BC. Judah's reigns laid end to end: 95 years, 5 past Jehu. On the calendar: Jehoshaphat reigned 3 years beside Asa, and Jehoram's and Ahaziah's first years were counted twice, and they too end at 841 BC. Ahab at Qarqar in 853 BC and Jehu's tribute in 841 BC are marked from the Assyrian records. Below, the arithmetic: 98 minus 8 is 90; 95 minus 3 minus 2 is 90; and Ahaziah's 2 plus Joram's 12 minus 2 is the 12 years between Qarqar and Jehu. A detail shows Nadab's two years falling between Asa's second year and his third (1 Kings 15:25, 28).
svg.text: The division of the kingdom to Jehu's revolt, in Israel's list and Judah's
as Kings numbers the reigns, laid end to end
as Kings numbers the reigns, laid end to end
− 8 first years that were also a predecessor's last
− 3 Jehoshaphat beside Asa − 2 years counted twice
931 to 841 BC is 90 years. Qarqar (853) to Jehu (841) is 12.
Nadab “began to reign … in the second year of Asa … and he reigned over Israel two years”
(1 Kings 15:25, ESV); Baasha killed him “in the third year of Asa” (1 Kings 15:28, ESV).
Two calendar years touched, two years counted. Where in each year the change fell is not stated.
After the manner of Clarence Larkin · the-way.lewy.au
